title: Residency decision lattice and stakeholder routing matrix for enterprise region & failover requests
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise sales and account teams regularly submit ad hoc requests for new region availability, strict data residency, or deterministic failover topologies. The current intake is inconsistent: some requests land as feature asks, others as contract addenda, and routing to engineering/security/legal is manual. This ticket creates a single decision lattice and routing matrix that product and sales can use to classify incoming requests, produce a deterministic outcome (approve / backlog / contracted rollout / require private deployment), and surface required artifacts to downstream teams.

Scope: Decision lattice covers: (1) new region provisioning requests, (2) data residency & residency exception requests, (3) deterministic failover/topology requirements (e.g., primary-region-only reads, cross-border failover bans), and (4) multi-region performance SLAs tied to enterprise contracts. Deliverable is a triage rubric + stakeholder routing matrix + templated request form for sales/CS + one-page summary for legal/ops.

Out of scope: Non-enterprise self-serve region preferences, infra capacity planning tasks, and low-touch developer sandbox region requests. Those continue to use existing self-serve flows.
acceptance_criteria: A concise decision lattice (visual + text) that classifies any incoming enterprise region/residency/failover request into one of four outcomes with <= 5 decision nodes
A stakeholder routing matrix that maps each outcome to owning teams and required artifacts (security, legal, infra, account exec, solutions engineering)
A templated intake form (Google Form + spreadsheet) for Sales/CS and a sample email template for customers
A published Confluence page with the rubric, routing matrix, and example decision traces for at least 6 historical requests
Product, Legal, Security, and Infra have reviewed and provided sign-off (comments or approvals in Confluence)
triage_scoring_rules: Score components and suggested weights: Customer ARR (30%), Data classification & sensitivity (25%), Regulatory/residency/legal constraint (20%), Latency/availability importance (10%), Engineering effort estimate / infra cost (15%).

Mapping of score ranges to outcomes: 0-30 -> Backlog / Self-serve guidance; 31-60 -> Prioritized roadmap candidate; 61-80 -> Contracted Dedicated / Private deployment evaluation; 81-100 -> Immediate enterprise onboarding + SLA/contract negotiation.
Hard gates: any request that requires physical on-premise or air-gapped deployment must route to Private deployment channel immediately (overrides score).
Failover gating: synchronous-read-only or single-region-only constraints require an infra feasibility assessment before approval; route to ENG with 'high' priority and estimated lead time.
routing_matrix: Outcome: Backlog / Guidance -> Owner: Product (PM) + Docs -> Artifacts: recommended self-serve docs, region availability page link
Outcome: Roadmap Candidate -> Owner: Product (PM) + Sales -> Artifacts: business case doc, prioritized in quarterly planning
Outcome: Contracted Dedicated/Private Eval -> Owner: Solutions Eng + Sales + Legal + Security -> Artifacts: NDA/contract language, KMS/HSM requirements, SOC/ISO mapping
Outcome: Immediate Onboarding (SLA) -> Owner: Partner Eng + Infra SRE + Legal -> Artifacts: capacity commit, runbook, rollback/fallback plan, support escalation path
decision_examples: Example 1: 10M ARR healthcare customer requires EU-only residency and audited log retention -> Score 78 -> Contracted Dedicated eval; route to Solutions Eng and Legal; Security to prepare controls checklist.

Example 2: Series B startup wants low-latency APAC region for better UX but no residency demands -> Score 42 -> Roadmap Candidate; include in next regional demand bundle if aggregated with 3 other customers.

Example 3: Large fintech requires multi-region geo-failover with no cross-border failover allowed -> Hard gate triggers Private deployment assessment regardless of score; Security & Legal sign-off required.

Example 4: Small PoC customer asks to pin model serving to a different region for testing -> Score 18 -> Backlog; provide self-serve instructions and recommend trial credits in requested region if available.
deliverables: Confluence page: 'Residency Decision Lattice & Routing Matrix' (published)
Google Form + Intake spreadsheet with automated scoring column
One-page sales playbook + customer email templates
Review notes and sign-offs from Security, Legal, Infra, and PM
Rollout plan for internal comms and Sales training (30 minute session + FAQ)
